label: Resource-extraction frontier / boom economy
description: Recurring nineteenth-century pattern in which discoveries of gold, silver, and other extractive opportunities triggered rapid migration, speculative investment, service economies, boomtowns, infrastructure, environmental change, and intensified encounters with existing communities. Nevada silver and the Klondike are specific cases rather than separate universal forces.

label: Settler-community formation in the American West
description: Recurring process of migration, town-building, farming, ranching, transportation, state formation, and land acquisition as U.S. settlement expanded westward. The process was culturally plural and frequently involved Indigenous dispossession, earlier Spanish and Mexican communities, Black migration, immigrant labor, and conflicts over land and power.

label: Industrial agriculture & migrant labor
culture: United States / especially western commercial agriculture
description: Large-scale commercial agriculture organized around concentrated land and capital, seasonal harvests, mobile labor forces, packing and transport systems, and unequal labor markets. California's Salinas Valley is one specific case, with Mexican, Filipino, white, Chinese, and other workers participating in different periods and roles.

label: Journalism as writer formation
description: Professional reporting, newspaper and magazine writing, deadlines, observation, interviewing, compression, fact gathering, and audience awareness as a recurring formation pathway for literary writers. The pattern should be represented through specific newsrooms, careers, and creator testimony rather than assumed for every writer who published journalism.
